messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbuscloud.com>, Kevin Patel <kevin.patel@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: NimbusCloud CISO <security@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR prep: NimbusCloud customer health + renewal risk register — exec flags

Team & Nimbus sponsors,

We're starting QBR prep for NimbusCloud (renewal due 2026-04-15). Attached is the living risk register and a health-slide deck I pulled together — please review and update the risk register row assigned to you by EOD Monday (2026-02-23). High-level asks: 

- Laura: update usage / cost variance commentary and any outstanding action items from CS/Solutions.
- Markus: flag any product or infra incidents that would require executive attention; mark severity on the register.
- Rishi: finance needs an updated renewal forecast and recommended concession band (if any).
- Stephanie: confirm if SOC2 artifacts we shared last quarter need refresh or if Nimbus requested additional evidence.
- Asha / Kevin (Nimbus): confirm the list of stakeholders who will attend the March 9 QBR and any new agenda items.

Executive attention items I already flagged in the register: potential data residency ask from their EU business, and an unplanned 15% spike in token usage in Jan that pushed their costs over forecast. If either of those escalate, we should be prepared to propose a short-term credit or a committed capacity adjustment.

Please use the attached Excel as the canonical source — I will roll it up into the QBR pack after updates. If you need a 15-minute sync, reply with availability; otherwise, I'll assume asynchronous updates.

Attachments: QBR_Risk_Register_NimbusCloud_20260220.xlsx, NimbusCloud_Health_Slides_20260220.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
555-0198

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR prep: NimbusCloud customer health + renewal risk register — exec flags

Marissa — thank you for pulling this together. Quick notes (I've edited the register and attached supporting slides):

- Usage/Cost: NimbusCloud did a multi-region load test 01/14–01/16 which explains the 15% token spike; they confirmed the spike is not expected to repeat but it does reduce their budget runway. I added a note with the load-test logs and linked the internal ticket (CS-984).
- Open action: Solutions owes a follow-up on query optimization recommendations (ticket SOL-411). I've put a target completion date of 2026-02-26.
- Adoption: their ML Platform team has started piloting the embeddings endpoint for semantic search (pilot flagged as green).
- Contacts: Asha will bring product and Kevin will represent procurement/renewals. Asked them to confirm folks for March 9.

I attached a one-page health slide that calls out the usage spike and the pending optimization action. No additional SOC2 asks surfaced in our last sync — Stephanie, can you confirm whether the artifact list in the register is sufficient?

Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
[Attachment stub: NimbusCloud_Health_Slides_20260220.pdf]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbuscloud.com>, Kevin Patel <kevin.patel@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR prep: NimbusCloud customer health + renewal risk register — exec flags

Folks — I reviewed the updated register. Two items I think require immediate exec visibility: 

1) EU data residency ask: their legal has started drafting a contract addendum that would require hosting a dedicated private deployment in eu-west-1. This is scope-and-cost significant; we should prepare an estimated TCO (3-year) and a go/no-go decision window.

2) Budget shock: if we do not propose a mitigation (credit or committed capacity), procurement has signaled they may push renewal to a competitive RFP. I recommend we offer a one-quarter credit tied to a short-term commitment and include a clear migration/rightsizing plan.

Action items:
- Marissa/Laura: prepare a one-pager that summarizes the ask + recommended concession and impacts by 2026-02-25 COB.
- Rishi: please run a sensitivity on ARR with and without a 10–20% concession and share by EOD 2026-02-24.
- Stephanie: confirm whether SOC2+KMS evidence is fully current for an EU private deployment; escalate gaps by 2026-02-24.

Markus
VP, Sales Operations
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Acknowledged — I'm running three scenarios and will upload the sensitivity table to the register:

A) Baseline (no concession): renewal at list price, 85% probability.
B) Small concession (10% one-quarter credit): renewal probability +8 points.
C) Committed capacity (12-month commit discount): renewal probability +18 points, but increases near-term ARR certainty.

I'll have numbers and recommended option by EOD 2026-02-24. Marissa/Laura — happy to join a quick call to walk the execs through the financials on 2026-02-25 between 09:00–11:00 PST if that helps.

Rishi Malhotra
